That very singular man, old Doctor Heidegger, once invited four venerable friends to meet him in his study, where he intended to conduct a peculiar experiment. <break time="0.8s" /> There were three white bearded gentlemen, Mister Medbourne, Colonel Killigrew, and Mister Gascoigne, and a withered lady whose name was the Widow Wycherly. <break time="0.8s" /> Mister Medbourne, in the vigor of his age, had been a prosperous merchant, but he had lost everything through a frantic speculation and was now little better than a beggar. <break time="0.8s" /> Colonel Killigrew had wasted his best years, his health, and his fortune in the pursuit of sinful pleasures, which had left him with a body tormented by gout. <break time="0.8s" /> Mister Gascoigne was a ruined politician, a man of evil fame, who had been so completely forgotten that the present generation scarcely knew his name. <break time="0.8s" /> As for the Widow Wycherly, she had been a great beauty in her day, but scandalous stories had driven her from society, and she now lived in deep seclusion. <break time="0.8s" /> It is worth mentioning that each of the three old gentlemen had once been on the point of cutting the others throats for her sake. <break time="0.8s" /> Before going further, we must also say that Doctor Heidegger and all his guests were commonly thought to be a little out of their minds.

The study was a dim, old fashioned chamber, festooned with cobwebs and sprinkled with antique dust, where tall bookcases of oak lined the walls. <break time="0.8s" /> Over the central bookcase stood a bronze bust of Hippocrates, with which, according to some authorities, Doctor Heidegger was accustomed to consult in all difficult cases. <break time="0.8s" /> In the darkest corner hung a tall, narrow mirror, within which, it was fabled, the spirits of all the doctors dead patients dwelt. <break time="0.8s" /> The opposite side of the room was ornamented with the portrait of a young lady who, many years before, had been on the point of marrying Doctor Heidegger. <break time="0.8s" /> But, being affected with some slight disorder, she had swallowed one of her lovers prescriptions and died on the bridal evening. <break time="0.8s" /> The greatest curiosity of the study was a ponderous book, bound in black leather, which was well known to be a book of magic. <break time="0.8s" /> On the summer afternoon of our tale, a round table stood in the middle of the room, and on it was placed a cut glass vase of beautiful form. <break time="0.8s" /> The sunshine came through the window and fell upon the vase, so that a mild splendor was reflected from it onto the ashen faces of the five old people.
